plans.buy_case: MNST is exhibiting classic mean-reversion setup: RSI 37 (oversold), price hugging lower Bollinger Band with active squeeze, and confirmed above 200MA with golden cross intact. Volume surge + low VIX complacency suggests institutional accumulation into weakness—ideal swing entry for a quality defensive name.
plans.entry_condition: Wait for RSI to dip into 25-30 zone OR price to touch lower BB (-2σ) on the next intraday dip. Do NOT chase at current RSI 37—you want better risk/reward. This is a 3-5 day patience play.
plans.exit_condition: Take profit at RSI 65-70 or upper BB touch (~$96.50). Hard stop: close below 200MA ($81.19) or RSI falls back below 30 on a failed bounce—signals broken support.
plans.risk: Insufficient fundamental data is your biggest red flag. MNST is healthy by reputation, but you don't have recent earnings, guidance, or competitive moat confirmation. Low VIX can flip fast—if broader market corrects, defensives don't always hold. Position sizing ($90) is appropriate for this uncertainty.
plans.note_for_busy_student: This is a textbook swing setup, but don't force entry at RSI 37. Set alerts for $88.50 and $89.00; check once daily. If it doesn't trigger within 2 weeks, the thesis is broken—move on. Good discipline beats impatience.

plans.buy_case: D is hitting a Bollinger Band squeeze with RSI in oversold territory (39.2) while price holds above the 200MA—textbook mean-reversion setup. The golden cross (50MA > 200MA) provides a technical tailwind, and above-average volume suggests institutional interest in the dip. However, lack of near-term catalysts and the low-VIX environment (complacency risk) cap conviction—this is a tactical bounce trade, not a fundamental conviction play.
plans.entry_condition: Wait for RSI to drop to 30–32 range OR price to touch the lower Bollinger Band (≈$66.20). Do not chase at current price; discipline matters with only $4,581 capital.
plans.exit_condition: Take profits at RSI >70 or price touches upper BB (~$69.80). Hard stop at RSI >75 (overextended) or breach below 200MA ($62.59)—if the golden cross breaks, thesis is invalidated.
plans.risk: Utilities are defensive and slow movers—D could grind sideways instead of mean-revert sharply. VIX complacency may signal a broader market pullback that drags the sector. Single-share position limits profit, but that's appropriate given portfolio size.

plans.buy_case: Classic mean-reversion setup: RSI 33.3 + price kissing lower Bollinger Band with MACD turning up suggests a bounce is likely. Price sitting right at 200MA with golden cross intact provides technical support, and elevated volume confirms institutional interest in the dip.
plans.entry_condition: Wait for RSI to cross above 35 OR price to touch the lower BB ($67.80–$68.00 range). Do NOT chase at current levels.
plans.exit_condition: Take profit at RSI 65+ OR upper Bollinger Band (~$71.50). Hard stop: close if price breaks below 200MA ($66.05) with volume—signals breakdown of support structure.

plans.advisor_note: **SKIP THIS TRADE.** Your signal tier flags 'Avoid' for good reason. Yes, technicals are textbook, but EIX's deteriorating fundamentals + regulatory/wildfire risks make this a mean-reversion trap disguised as an oversold bounce. The $69 position size is too small to justify the opportunity cost. Instead, wait for a utilities-sector leader (NEE, DUK) to trigger the same RSI/BB setup, or deploy capital into growth plays where your edge is sharper. A busy MIT student should trade setups with conviction, not edge cases. Pass.

plans.advisor_note: Skip this one unless RSI hits 28-30 AND you see fresh positive news on the utility or rates outlook. The 'Avoid' signal tier + deteriorating fundamentals is a red flag. Your edge as a swing trader relies on mean-reversion into fundamentally sound names. This feels like catching a falling knife. Wait for better risk/reward or a stronger quality name.

plans.buy_case: CNP is flashing classic mean-reversion setup: RSI 32.5 (oversold), price pinned to lower Bollinger Band, MACD inflecting upward, and anchored above 200MA with golden cross intact. Low VIX (14.9) suggests complacency, which often precedes utility sector rotation into defensive names—CNP's dividend yield makes it attractive on bounces.
plans.entry_condition: Wait for RSI to dip to 28–30 range OR price to touch lower BB ($39.80–$40.00) on next pullback. Do not chase at current $40.68. Volume confirmation on entry is critical given low volatility regime.
plans.exit_condition: Sell 50% at $42.50 (2.1 week MA resistance); stop loss at $39.20 (break below 200MA support). Exit remaining position if RSI crosses above 65 without follow-through volume, or if CNP gaps below 200MA on negative news.
plans.timeframe: 3–6 weeks. Utilities move slowly; this is a modest swing, not a home run.
plans.risk: Utilities are rate-sensitive; any hawkish Fed pivot or rising bond yields will kill this trade. Fundamental 'neutral' health is a red flag—verify no upcoming earnings misses or dividend cuts before entry. VIX complacency also means sharp reversals are possible if macro sentiment shifts.
